The Arizona Department of Environmental Quality (ADEQ) has issued a
PM-10 High Pollution Advisory for Pinal County through Saturday.

An episode of strong and gusty winds is forecast to generate
widespread blowing dust that may result in local PM-10 concentrations
that pose a health risk. Adverse health effects increase as air
quality deteriorates.

Coarse particulate matter - also known as PM-10 - is an air
contaminant that can aggravate heart and lung disease conditions,
especially in older adults, children, and those with asthma. A
decrease in physical activity is recommended.

Consolidate your travel, stabilize loose soils, slow down or avoid
travel on dirt roads, reduce or eliminate fireplace use, and avoid
using gas-powered lawn equipment.

For details on this High Pollution Advisory, visit the ADEQ internet
site at www.azdeq.gov/forecast/WestPinal or call 602-771-2300.

properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued August 28 at 2:15PM AST by NWS San Juan PR
properties.description:
ESFSJU

The National Hurricane Center issued the last advisory on Dolly,
located nearly 1200 miles southeast of the local islands. This
tropical wave will reach the area on Sunday and Monday.

Since the system is expected to find a hostile environment, a
widespread and long-lasting rainfall event is not anticipated.
Instead, squally weather will bring periods of moderate to locally
heavy rainfall, beginning late Sunday and stretching into Monday. In
general, we are anticipating rainfall accumulations of 1 to 3 inches,
which will be beneficial for any areas receiving the rain. Lingering
moisture from the remnants of Dolly could contribute to additional
showers developing on Tuesday. The risk of flooding is low to locally
medium. Areas with the drainage system clogged by death vegetation
debris or urbanized areas with poor drainage could experience
localized flooding.

Any rainfall will be welcome, and could bring a temporary relieve to
the ongoing severe to extreme drought plaguing Puerto Rico and the
Virgin Islands. However, the rain should not be enough to end the
drought.

At this time, the confidence in the forecast is medium, and the users
are advised to monitor the forecast in case changes are introduced.
If that the case, this product will be update accordingly.

NWSheadline: Beneficial rains from the remnants of Tropical Storm Dolly areexpected to reach Puerto Rico and the Virgin Islands on Sunday and Monday

properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued August 28 at 9:17AM AST by NWS San Juan PR
properties.description:
ESFSJU

The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical Storm
Dolly, located nearly 1200 miles southeast of the local islands. The
official forecast calls for Dolly to degenerate into a tropical wave
before reaching the area on Sunday and Monday.

Since the system is expected to find a hostile environment, a
widespread and long-lasting rainfall event is not anticipated.
Instead, squally weather will bring periods of moderate to locally
heavy rainfall, beginning late Sunday and stretching into Monday. In
general, we are anticipating rainfall accumulations of 1 to 3 inches,
which will be beneficial for any areas receiving the rain. Lingering
moisture from the remnants of Dolly could contribute to additional
showers developing on Tuesday. The risk of flooding is low to locally
medium. Areas with the drainage system clogged by death vegetation
debris or urbanized areas with poor drainage could experience
localized flooding.

Any rainfall will be welcome, and could bring a temporary relieve to
the ongoing severe to extreme drought plaguing Puerto Rico and the
Virgin Islands. However, the rain should not be enough to end the
drought.

At this time, the confidence in the forecast is medium, and the users
are advised to monitor the forecast in case changes are introduced.
If that the case, this product will be update accordingly.

NWSheadline: Beneficial rains from the remnants of Tropical Storm Dolly are expected to reach Puerto Rico and the Virgin Islands on Sunday and Monday

Yentna at Lake Creek. River rises from this storm will likely be
less than was observed following the Tuesday storm.

* Many lower locations along rivers such as gravel bars and other
spots popular for camping and recreating may become inundated with
water with rivers reaching bankfull conditions.

* Heavy rain may result in localized ponding in low-lying areas and
locations with poor drainage.

Next Steps:

* Residents along area streams as well as river users and recreators
should anticipate higher than normal water levels and are advised
to monitor weather and river forecasts.

* Send weather or flooding reports to inws.ncep.noaa.gov/report/ or
by calling 1-907-266-5127.

* Reports on river conditions may be sent to the river forecast
center by calling 1-907-266-5160.
